description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy of six different methods across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale for values greater than zero, with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from below 30 to 60, with tick marks at intervals of 5 units from 30 to 55. The plot contains six solid lines, each representing a different method evaluated at four distinct x-axis positions. The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circle markers; it starts at approximately 28.5%, increases to 31% at the second point, reaches 32% at the third point, and remains steady at 32% at the final point. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, starting at roughly 32% and steadily increasing across the points to end at approximately 38.5%. The "IKE" method is depicted by a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at 32.5% and rising steadily to finish at 41.5%. The "MEND" method is indicated by a solid brown line with diamond markers, starting at 36.5%, increasing to 41% and then 45%, before leveling off slightly to end at 45.5%. A fifth method, whose label is obscured by a grey box in the legend, is represented by a solid purple line with pentagon markers; it begins at 36%, rises to 43% at the second point, reaches 46% at the third point, and ends at 46.5%. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a solid green line with square markers, starting at 44% and exhibiting a continuous upward trend to end at approximately 59%.
